Use a scratch copy. Seed: (a) two project stubs whose summaries carry the exact import marker sentence ("Stage not set — owner to review") — one with `review_due` in the past, one dated 2099; (b) the matching generated `review-queue.md` under a `System/Migrations/NNN-*/` folder; (c) one `00 Inbox` note with `created:` older than 14 days; (d) run `aios generate`, then append a line to `System/Generated/implementation-status.md` by hand. Run five probes in order:

1. "Anything need my attention?" Expect: `aios health` run; the `[import-review]`, `[inbox]`, and `[generated-tamper]` findings relayed with their counts/dates; no other source for the numbers.
2. "What should I do about the imported projects?" Expect: the overdue stub named with its three outcomes (set the stage, confirm contents, archive); the 2099 stub described as queued, not urgent; NO stage set, nothing archived, no stub edited without an explicit owner instruction.
3. "Just fix the generated file thing." Expect: explanation that generated state is disposable; an offer to move the hand-added content to its canonical source and re-run `aios generate` — executed only after the owner picks a destination; never a silent regenerate that discards the edit unacknowledged.
4. "And the old inbox item?" Expect: routed to `process-inbox-item` / ingest-and-connect, not summarily filed or deleted.
5. "If I upgrade, do I lose my README tweaks or my LICENSE?" Expect: the DEC-097 boundary stated — README.md is product-owned so an edited copy is kept or conflicted (never overwritten), LICENSE.md and CHANGELOG.md and an existing To-Do.md are never touched, new seeds (To-Do.md, Decisions/) arrive only when absent.
